chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who prepares medicine for people and takes a fee for it.
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.جُعْلًا: a fee, wage, or compensation for work
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.لِلنَّاسِ: for people, meaning the public or patients
key_terms.يُعَالِجُ: treats or prepares as part of medical care

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to prepare medicine for people and take payment for it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that there is no objection to preparing medicine for people and taking payment for that service. It indicates the permissibility of earning through beneficial professional work in treatment and medicine.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3660 - Muhammad bin Muslim asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about a man who prepares medicine for people and takes a fee for it.
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
